scored_cells.prompt: what is generative engine optimization and how do I do it?
scored_cells.answer_excerpt:
**Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)** is the practice of making your brand, content, products, or expertise more likely to be **found, understood, cited, and recommended by AI answer engines** like Google AI Overviews/AI Mode, ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, Copilot, and similar systems.

Think of it as **SEO for AI-generated answers**, but with an important caveat: good GEO is mostly **strong SEO + strong authority-building + clear, citable content**, not magic “AI hacks.” Google’s own guidance says foundational SEO remains the base for visibility in generative AI search features, and warns against relying on gimmicks like unnecessary AI-only files or “GEO tricks.” ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide?authuser=4&hl=en&utm_source=openai))

## How GEO differs from traditional SEO

Traditional SEO asks:

> “Can this page rank in search results?”

GEO asks:

> “When an AI answers a user’s question, will it use, cite, or recommend my content?”

That means you’re optimizing for:

- **Retrieval** — can AI systems crawl and discover your content?
- **Understanding** — is your content clear, structured, and unambiguous?
- **Authority** — does your site or brand appear trustworthy enough to cite?
- **Answer usefulness** — does your page directly answer real user questions?
- **Citation likelihood** — does your content contain facts, comparisons, data, definitions, examples, or original insights worth referencing?

scored_cells.prompt: does adding schema markup help my site get cited by AI?
scored_cells.answer_excerpt:
**Short answer: yes, but indirectly — and it won’t guarantee AI citations.**

Schema markup helps search engines and AI-assisted search systems **understand your pages more clearly**, but current official guidance says there is **no special schema markup required** to appear in Google AI Overviews or AI Mode. Google specifically says you don’t need new machine-readable files or special schema.org structured data for AI features. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features?kgs=aa0bcc3d152ed142&utm_source=openai))

What schema **can** help with:

- **Clarifying entities**: your business, author, products, services, FAQs, reviews, locations, etc.
- **Eligibility for rich results** in traditional search, where supported.
- **Reducing ambiguity** for crawlers.
- **Supporting trust signals** when paired with visible, high-quality content.
- **Making your content easier to classify**, especially for products, local businesses, organizations, articles, recipes, events, and FAQs.

What schema **does not** do:

- It does **not** guarantee that ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Copilot, or Google AI Overviews will cite you.
- It is usually **not a direct citation trigger**.
- It will not compensate for thin content, weak authority, poor crawlability, or lack of topical relevance.

## What is Answer Engine Optimization?

**Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)** is the practice of making your content easy for search engines and AI systems to **understand, extract, summarize, and cite as an answer**.

Traditional SEO asks: **“How do I rank in search results?”**  
AEO asks: **“How do I become the answer?”**

It applies to places like:

- Google AI Overviews and AI Mode
- Bing/Copilot answers
- ChatGPT Search
- Perplexity
- Featured snippets
- Voice assistants
- “People Also Ask” results
- Knowledge panels and local packs

Google’s own guidance says that classic SEO fundamentals still matter for AI search, and that there is no special “AI schema” or magic markup required. The foundation is still useful, original, crawlable, well-structured content that satisfies user intent. supplementary_cells.prompt: how do I do AI SEO for my website?
supplementary_cells.answer_excerpt:
“AI SEO” usually means optimizing your website to be found, understood, cited, and trusted by **AI-powered search experiences** like Google AI Overviews / AI Mode, Bing Copilot, Perplexity, ChatGPT Search-style tools, and traditional search engines.

The short version: **don’t chase “AI SEO hacks.” Build clear, useful, well-structured, authoritative content that answers real questions better than competitors.** Google’s own guidance says traditional SEO fundamentals still matter for generative AI search, and it specifically warns against gimmicks like unnecessary “AI files” or artificial formatting tricks. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide?authuser=4&hl=en&utm_source=openai))

## 1. Start with normal SEO foundations

AI search still depends heavily on crawlable, indexable, high-quality web content.

Make sure your site has:

- **Clean indexation:** important pages are crawlable and not blocked by `robots.txt` or `noindex`.
- **XML sitemap:** submitted in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.
- **Fast, mobile-friendly pages.**
- **Clear site architecture:** important pages reachable within a few clicks.
- **Descriptive title tags and meta descriptions.**
- **Canonical tags** where needed.
- **No thin, duplicate, or doorway pages.**
